text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Another round of fuel shortage hits Lagos and nearby Oyo states; 26.5 million litres of petrol expected in Lagos on Saturday.
- Central bank mops up 14.9 billion naira from circulation.
- Nigeria Airways staff held over theft of digital computer of the national carrier's A 310 aircraft granted bail.
- United Bank for Africa, one of Nigeria's top three, embarks on computerisation of its operations.
- Lagos chief judge Omotunde Ilori decongests prisons by freeing 118 detainees.
- Opposition NADECO group rejects plans by political parties and government to shift state elections to 1998 from this year.
- State oil firm can't explain fresh fuel scarcity in Lagos.
- Detained presidential claimant Moshood Abiola is now more religious and sober, according to his doctor Ore Falomo, who saw him recently.
- Negotiations to lift mutual ban on each other's aircraft by Nigeria and Britain stalls as British expert due in Lagos to check Nigeria Airways planes for safety is denied visa.
- Plans have reached advanced stage to bring in Israeli doctors to work with the Nigerian Eye Foundation.
